note: priority 1 = check weekly, 2 = monthly, 3 = quarterly. Used by tools/update_queue.py to order the update crawl.

labs.name: CMU Robotics Institute
labs.notes: DAgger and the imitation-learning theory lineage; 3D Diffuser Actor; Pathak/Gupta labs on scalable embodied learning and the WHIRL/VideoDex human-video-to-robot line.

labs.name: Figure AI
labs.notes: Helix dual-system (S1/S2) humanoid VLA. Closed-source; announcements come via blog/video rather than papers.

labs.name: Google DeepMind — Robotics
labs.notes: Absorbed Google Brain Robotics & Everyday Robots. Origin of the RT-* line, SayCan, PaLM-E, Gemini Robotics, the Dreamer and Genie lines.

labs.name: Hugging Face — LeRobot
labs.notes: De-facto open-source hub: reimplementations of ACT/Diffusion Policy/π0, SmolVLA, standardized dataset format, cheap SO-100/SO-101 arms.

labs.name: MIT CSAIL / Improbable AI
labs.notes: Tedrake's group (Diffusion Policy co-author, Drake) and Pulkit Agrawal's Improbable AI on sim-to-real dexterity.

labs.name: NVIDIA GEAR Lab / Robotics
labs.notes: GR00T humanoid foundation models, Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim, Cosmos world foundation models, Eureka reward design.

labs.name: Physical Intelligence (π)
labs.notes: Founded 2024 by Levine, Hausman, Finn et al. Flow-matching VLAs (π0 line), the openpi release, FAST action tokenizer.

labs.name: Stanford IRIS (Chelsea Finn)
labs.notes: ALOHA / ACT, Mobile ALOHA, OpenVLA co-author, meta-learning roots. Tightly coupled to Physical Intelligence.

labs.name: Stanford REALab (Shuran Song)
labs.notes: Diffusion Policy and UMI originated with this group (formerly Columbia CAIR). Focus on scalable data collection hardware.

labs.name: Stanford Vision & Learning Lab (Fei-Fei Li, Jiajun Wu)
labs.notes: VoxPoser, ReKep, BEHAVIOR benchmark suite. Zero-shot manipulation via foundation-model grounding.

labs.name: Toyota Research Institute — Robotics
labs.notes: Co-developer of Diffusion Policy; Large Behavior Models (LBM) program with rigorous statistical evaluation.

labs.name: UC Berkeley — RAIL (Sergey Levine)
labs.notes: SAC, Octo, BridgeData, SERL/HIL-SERL, DayDreamer, embodied chain-of-thought. The single densest source of robot-RL methodology.

labs.name: UT Austin — Robot Perception & Learning (Yuke Zhu)
labs.notes: robomimic, RoboCasa, LIBERO — the benchmark backbone of the field. Joint appointment with NVIDIA GEAR.

labs.name: 1X Technologies
labs.notes: NEO humanoid; published a learned world model used as an evaluator for policies.

labs.name: AgiBot / 智元机器人
labs.notes: AgiBot World — one of the largest open real-robot manipulation datasets; GO-1 policy family.

labs.name: Allen Institute for AI (PRIOR)
labs.notes: Molmo VLM with pointing supervision — a common grounding front-end for manipulation. THOR/ProcTHOR simulators.

labs.name: Amazon FAR (Frontier AI & Robotics)
labs.notes: Absorbed Covariant's founders and much of its team in 2024; warehouse-scale manipulation data.

labs.name: Boston Dynamics
labs.notes: Electric Atlas manipulation; partnership with Toyota Research Institute on large behavior models.

labs.name: ByteDance Seed / Research
labs.notes: GR-1 / GR-2 video-pretrained manipulation policies; strong video-generation crossover.

labs.name: Columbia — Creative Machines / CAIR
labs.notes: Birthplace of Diffusion Policy (Shuran Song's group before the Stanford move).

labs.name: Dyna Robotics
labs.notes: DYNA-1 model targeting long-duration autonomous dexterous tasks at commercial reliability. Also pursuing large-scale egocentric human-video data collection — confirm any scale claims against their own posts before citing them.

labs.name: Generalist AI
labs.notes: Founded by Pete Florence (ex-Google DeepMind); general-purpose dexterous manipulation foundation models.

labs.name: Georgia Tech (Danfei Xu, RIPL)
labs.notes: EgoMimic and the wearable-capture line: treating human egocentric data as another embodiment to co-train with, rather than something to retarget.

labs.name: Meta FAIR — Embodied AI
labs.notes: V-JEPA line, Habitat simulator, DINOv2/v3 backbones widely reused as robot visual encoders. Also the origin of Ego4D, Ego-Exo4D and Project Aria — the capture stack most human-data robotics runs on.

labs.name: NYU — GRAIL (Lerrel Pinto)
labs.notes: Behavior Transformers / VQ-BeT, cheap in-the-wild data collection rigs, on-robot fine-tuning, and the EgoZero line on training policies from human recordings with no robot data at all.

labs.name: OpenAI
labs.notes: Dactyl / ADR era defined sim-to-real dexterity; robotics team disbanded 2021 and restarted ~2024. PPO and CLIP remain load-bearing everywhere.

labs.name: RAI Institute (ex-Boston Dynamics AI Institute)
labs.notes: Marc Raibert's research institute; athletic intelligence and model-based + learned control.

labs.name: Shanghai AI Laboratory
labs.notes: SpatialVLA, InternVL backbones, OpenDriveLab collaboration on AgiBot World.

labs.name: Skild AI
labs.notes: CMU spinout (Deepak Pathak, Abhinav Gupta) pursuing an omni-bodied 'robot brain' across embodiments.

labs.name: Tesla — Optimus
labs.notes: End-to-end video-to-action policies reusing FSD infrastructure. No papers; track AI Day / earnings demos.

labs.name: Tsinghua University (AIR / TSAIL)
labs.notes: RDT-1B bimanual diffusion transformer; strong diffusion-model theory group feeding robot policies.

labs.name: UC Berkeley AUTOLab (Ken Goldberg)
labs.notes: Dex-Net grasping lineage; long-running work on reliable industrial-grade manipulation and data-driven grasping.

labs.name: UC San Diego (Hao Su, Xiaolong Wang)
labs.notes: ManiSkill / SAPIEN simulation stack; TD-MPC line; dexterous hand teleoperation and RL.

labs.name: University of Washington (Dieter Fox, Personal Robotics)
labs.notes: PerAct, RoboPoint, MuJoCo's origin (Todorov). Deep two-way traffic with NVIDIA Seattle robotics.

labs.name: Apple — Machine Learning Research
labs.notes: EgoDex and related egocentric dexterous-manipulation datasets captured on head-mounted consumer hardware with paired 3D hand pose.

labs.name: ETH Zurich — Robotic Systems Lab
labs.notes: Massively-parallel RL and sim-to-real methodology (ANYmal); the techniques transfer directly to arms and hands.

labs.name: Galbot / 银河通用
labs.notes: PKU-affiliated; synthetic-data-heavy grasping and mobile manipulation (GraspVLA, GroceryVLM).

labs.name: Imperial College London (Edward Johns)
labs.notes: RLBench benchmark; one-shot imitation and coarse-to-fine manipulation.

labs.name: Microsoft Research
labs.notes: CogACT and Magma lines; strong VLM pretraining feeding into embodied agents.

labs.name: Peking University (CoRe / Hao Dong)
labs.notes: Embodied perception and dexterous manipulation; closely tied to Galbot.

labs.name: TU Darmstadt — Intelligent Autonomous Systems (Jan Peters)
labs.notes: Movement primitives, policy search, and the classical robot-learning foundations much of modern IL rests on.

labs.name: Unitree Robotics
labs.notes: Hardware-first (G1/H1 humanoids, arms). Matters mainly as the cheap platform much open manipulation research now runs on.

labs.name: University of Freiburg (Abhinav Valada, Wolfram Burgard legacy)
labs.notes: CALVIN long-horizon language benchmark; HULC policies.

labs.name: X Square Robot / 自变量机器人
labs.notes: WALL-A / Wall-OSS end-to-end manipulation models with partial open-source releases.
